GROUPED ACQUISITION OF AN ADAPTIVE-RISK-COMPETITIVE QUADRATIC PREDICTOR

P1 continuation, independent acquisition companion, 30 October 2026 UTC.
This is an internally derived construction, not historical-priority clearance
or a claim of practical superiority. It changes the previous scalar-query
dependence on ambient dimension. It does not provide cheap acquisition of an
unknown Gaussian spectral model.

1. QUESTION AND ACCESS CONTRACT

An unknown real quadratic target on independent uniform signs is promised:

  f(x)=c+sum_i a_i x_i+sum_{i<j} b_ij x_i x_j,   x in {-1,1}^n.

The offline learner may submit a COMPLETE chosen Boolean vector and receive
its exact scalar value f(x). No coefficients, gradient, support list or
group-energy oracle is initially supplied. In deployment a fresh X has
independent uniform signs, and observing coordinate X_i costs one observation.
The comparison class contains every adaptive policy whose expected number
of distinct observations is at most k. Let R_ad(k) denote the infimal Bayes
squared prediction error in that class.

Chosen training evaluations and their complete input vectors are distinct
resources from observing coordinates of a deployed X. All must be charged.
In particular, a public simulator with chosen inputs does not give a direct
measurement of f(X) at an unknown deployed state.

For 0<epsilon<=1 and k>0, the construction below outputs a fixed coordinate
set S of size at most min(n,ceil(288 k/epsilon^2)) and a quadratic predictor
using only X_S. With probability at least1-alpha over offline acquisition,

  E[(f(X)-predictor(X_S))^2] <= (1+epsilon) R_ad(k).

The scalar-query count is

  O((1+k/epsilon^2)(1+log n)log(n/alpha)
      +(1+k/epsilon^2)^2+epsilon^(-1)log(1/alpha)),

before the optional full-interpolation fallback. No coefficient sparsity,
sign constraint, known active support or positive lower bound on nonzero
coefficients is assumed. Exact scalar values are substantive. Under noise,
the same group measurements have an explicit signal-floor cost, but the
purely multiplicative zero-risk conclusion is impossible uniformly; Section7
states this limitation instead of hiding it.

The proof combines ordinary Fourier/ANOVA machinery, a constructed positive
group-energy estimator, best-first tree search, a residual-dependent stopping
rule, and the preceding P1 risk comparison. Group testing itself is establish

COMPLETED ACQUISITION COMPANION

Files:
  PROOF.txt
  group_acquisition.py
  results.json

Reproduce from the workspace root:
  python p1_next/acquisition/group_acquisition.py

Claim established in the ordinary proof:
For an unknown promised real quadratic on independent uniform signs, exact
scalar membership queries suffice to acquire a fixed-coordinate predictor
whose MSE is at most (1+epsilon) times the informed optimal adaptive risk
with expected coordinate budget k, with probability at least 1-alpha. The
fixed set has at most min(n,ceil(288 k/epsilon^2)) coordinates. The deterministic
source-query budget is

  O((1+k/epsilon^2)(1+log n)log(n/alpha)
     +(1+k/epsilon^2)^2+epsilon^(-1)log(1/alpha)).

The important acquisition operation is explicitly constructed from four
scalar values: squared odd-group response plus squared independent internal-
group response difference has mean equal to additive coordinate influence.
Its variance is at most eight times the squared mean, including arbitrary
signs and dense interactions. The same four values give exact residual-energy
estimation. Best-first search plus a residual stop gives the displayed bound
without an unknown dynamic-range or minimum-nonzero-coefficient term. The
algorithm has an explicit expansion cap; exceeding it is a failed acquisition
event, impossible on the simultaneous calibration event. Intercept acquisition
uses the already constructed selected predictor to reduce its variance to the
remaining deployment risk.

Source promise and costs:
The target's quadratic form and the uniform independent deployment law are
assumed, not inferred from these tests. Chosen full Boolean inputs are stronger
than passive random examples. Every call pays n submitted signs and actual
target execution; exact tiny coefficients require adequate value precision.
The predictor pays O(L^2) coefficients. No cheap unknown Gaussian spectral
model acquisition or sublinear ambient-dimension running time follows.

Noise boundary:
An unbiased eight-raw-call group estimator with explicit signal-floor sample
cost is proved. A bounded-precision floor is also proved. A fully propagated
noisy additive-risk algorithm is NOT claimed. Uniform pure multiplicative
zero-risk learning is impossible with the stated nonzero readout error, even
for an unknown one-coordinate linear target.
